Commentary.Commentary: All eyes on Colombo now - That is it from this thrilling game, where England once again had to battle hard to get the points and seal qualification for the Super 8s, knocking Italy and Scotland out of contention. The action now moves from India to Sri Lanka, where Sri Lanka and Australia face off in Colombo in a clash that will shape Group B. That game gets underway shortly, with the hosts electing to bowl first, so you can simply switch tabs and enjoy all our coverage. Cheers!

The victorious skipper of England - Harry Brook starts by saying that they haven't played their best cricket but at the end of the day, they have made it through and are happy with it. Adds that it has been a bit of a trend for them in this tournament to let things slip with the bat but it is all about taking the right options. Brook reckons that they fielded really well and applauds the likes of Sam Curran and Will Jacks, who have stepped up in tricky situations. On giving Jofra Archer the extra over up top, Brook mentions that Jofra was on a heater at the start of the game and felt that they needed to make the most out of that fire and hence he was given 3 overs at the top. Ends by saying that they haven't been brave enough with the bat thus far and will look to do better as they now head to Sri Lanka.

The captain of Italy - Harry Manenti says they knew England were always going to come hard, and while Italy's plan to take wickets at regular intervals worked for a while, Will Jacks taking the game deep on a good batting surface made the difference. He feels England were about 15 to 20 runs above par in the end, and that proved costly. Manenti highlights the fight shown in the chase, especially the counter-attack from Benjamin Manenti and Justin Mosca, along with Grant Stewart's late surge, saying it reflects the belief growing within the group. He adds that pushing a top side like England so close gives Italy real confidence, even if they are still learning how to handle the big moments. Looking ahead, he says the focus now turns to the game against West Indies, where Italy will play with freedom and keep trying to show they belong at this level.
Time to hear from the captains now...

England hold on at the death - England made a strong start with the ball as Jofra Archer took two in his first over and Jamie Overton struck early as well. They then went quiet through the middle, with Liam Dawson tidy but Adil Rashid taken on despite picking up a wicket. The turning point was Will Jacks dismissing Benjamin Manenti, after which Sam Curran's excellent death bowling and Overton's three wickets got England over the line, though they will know they were pushed hard.

England's late overdrive - Electing to bat first, England posted a big total, but they had to work hard for it after slipping to 105 for 5 despite plenty of starts. Will Jacks then provided the late surge, just as he did against Nepal, smashing a 21-ball fifty, his maiden T20I half-century and the fastest by an English batter in a T20 World Cup, to lift England past 200. For Italy, Grant Stewart and Crishan Kalugamage picked up two wickets each but were expensive, while JJ Smuts was the standout with a tidy spell and a wicket. However, a costly final five overs, which went for 78, allowed England to run away with the momentum and that ultimately proved to be the difference.

A counter-attack that nearly stunned England - Not many would have given Italy a chance after England posted 202, but this World Cup has shown time and again that any team can challenge anyone. Italy lost three quick wickets early, but they refused to go away, launching a stunning counter-attack through Benjamin Manenti's incredible hitting and Justin Mosca's composure as the pair added 92 off 48 balls to haul them back into the contest. Manenti's dismissal for a 25-ball 60 came at a bad time and stalled the momentum, but Grant Stewart reignited the chase with a fiery 45 off 23. In the end, though, the target proved just a little too much for Italy to overhaul.

PLAYER OF THE MATCH - Will Jacks wins the award for his unbeaten 53 off 22 and the all important wicket of Benjamin Manenti. He says that they had spoken about keeping their intent up and knew it was a fast scoring ground, so they didn't quite know what a defendable score here was. On scoring his maiden T20I fifty, he says he feels happy to have gotten the half-century today and says that it was a long time coming. Further adds that there have been a few role changes for him and he is now settling nicely into this finisher role. On Benjamin Manenti's wicket, Jacks mentions that Manenti played really well, better than the English batters and he just tried to bowl full and straight to him, hoping for him to mishit one, which did happen. Adds that they now move to Sri Lanka, different conditions and feels that they need to adapt quickly to the challenge.

Italy win hearts, England take points - England have survived another scare in this World Cup, just about getting over the line to confirm their place in the Super 8s, though not in the most convincing fashion. Credit must go to Italy, who produced a tremendous fight, forcing Harry Brook into a few uncomfortable moments along the way, but while the decisive moments did not fall their way, they can certainly hold their heads high.

Commentary.Commentary: SIX! Oh, Rashid starts with a gift and Harry Manenti dispatches it into the stands. The slider on middle, but it is just too short. Manenti hangs back and slogs it powerfully beyond the mid-wicket fence. The 50 is also up for Italy.

Commentary.Commentary: DRINKS! No shortage of entertainment in the Powerplay. England managed to pick up the 3 wickets, but Italy finished well, getting 25 runs in the last two overs. Justin Mosca looks in great touch and has taken a liking to Archer, while Benjamin Manenti will be looking to join the fun as well. In the context of the game, England are much ahead and will look to keep chipping away at the wickets, especially with the field restrictions now lifted. Here is Adil Rashid to bowl after the break.

FOUR! Fractionally short and Justin Mosca is all over it. Short and around off, Mosca hops back and cuts it firmly between point and covers and the ball races away to the fence. Italy finish the Powerplay strongly, getting 13 runs off this over, ending with 47/3 in 6 overs.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.6: Will Jacks to Justin Mosca, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Jacks comes around the wicket to the left-hander, lands it full and on middle. Justin Mosca blocks it off.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.5: Will Jacks to Justin Mosca, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Dragged length around off, Ben comes forward and pushes it into the off side and the batters scamper through for the single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.4: Will Jacks to Benjamin Manenti, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: More turn for Jacks. On a length, on middle, turns into the pads, Manenti fails to get it away.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.3: Will Jacks to Benjamin Manenti, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR MORE! Floated up outside off, Manenti throws his hands at it and slices it over Jofra Archer at short third and the ball rolls away into the fence behind.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.2: Will Jacks to Benjamin Manenti, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Turn for Jacks but the line is all wrong. Shorter, on middle and leg, turns down the leg side. Benjamin Manenti shovels it down past short fine leg and picks up a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.1: Will Jacks to Benjamin Manenti, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Justin Mosca is putting on a show, hitting Jofra Archer for as many as 5 boundaries in the space of 8 balls. Will Jacks now comes in to bowl the last over of the Powerplay.
FOUR! Fantastic shot! Jofra Archer sticks to the shorter length, but bowls this just around off. Justin Mosca backs away to free his arms and cuts it over point for four more runs.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.6: Jofra Archer to Justin Mosca, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Pitched up and on off, Justin Mosca pushes it to short cover.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Put away! Jofra Archer bowls this into the surface, on middle, but this is not short enough to trouble the batter. Justin Mosca climbs onto it quickly and pulls it to the deep mid-wicket fence for another boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.4: Jofra Archer to Justin Mosca, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Beauty! Hits the length hard and in that channel outside off, shaping away. Justin Mosca tries to play it from the crease but gets beaten on the outside edge.

Commentary.Commentary: Good length and on off, Justin Mosca pats it down to the off side.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.2: Jofra Archer to Justin Mosca, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Nice shot! Short of a length and well outside off. Justin Mosca gets the chance to free his hands and crunches it through point for a boudnary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.1: Jofra Archer to Justin Mosca, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Talk about anticipation from Jos Buttler, and England get their third wicket in the space of 4 overs. Benjamin Manenti replaces his brother, Harry Manenti and walks out at number 5 for Italy.

OUT! CAUGHT BEHIND! That is a stunning catch from Jos Buttler behind the stumps. Jamie Overton sees the batter move across to the off side, lands this on a shortish length and outside off. Harry Manenti shuffles across for the scoop but gets cramped up for the room and only manages to get it off the gloves. Buttler sees this and already moves to his left early. He times his jump to perfection and plucks it out of thin air with his outstretched right glove above his head, going across like a goalkeeper making a save. Italy are 22/3, chasing 203 runs.
Commentary.Howout: c Jos Buttler b Jamie Overton
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.6: Jamie Overton to Harry Manenti, OUT! c Jos Buttler b Jamie Overton.

Commentary.Commentary: Swing and a miss! Pitched up and on off, holds its line, Harry Manenti tries to smear it through covers but misses.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.5: Jamie Overton to Harry Manenti, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Full again and on middle, angling in, Harry Manenti clips it to short mid-wicket.

Commentary.Commentary: Good fielding! Goes fuller and around off, Harry Manenti opens the face of his bat and drives it square wide of backward point. Jacob Bethell dives to his right to save a certain boundary.

Commentary.Commentary: Bangs this into the pitch, outside off, gets some extra bounce. Harry Manenti chases after it but misses.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Hat-trick of boundaries for Italy! Short of a length and on middle. Harry Manenti picks up the length early. He rolls his wrists and pulls it away to the deep square leg fence for four more runs.

Commentary.Commentary: The artificial lights are now starting to take full effect at the Eden Gardens and Italy are also just starting to find their feet in this colossal run chase.
FOUR! Two in two! Jofra Archer just errs in line a bit and bowls this full, angling down the leg side. Justin Mosca flicks it away nicely to the deep fine leg fence for another boundary.

It takes the top edge and flies towards deep square leg. Phil Salt runs to his right, leaps and tries to grab and push it back in but fails to do so and the ball goes over the fence for a biggie.

Commentary.Commentary: England end the first over with more wickets than runs given away. The new batter, Harry Manenti, will be at the non-striker's end now. Meanwhile, it will be Jamie Overton to share the new ball with Archer.

OUT! EDGED AND GONE! Double strike from Jofra Archer and he is loving life in Kolkata. This is a back-of-a-length delivery, in that channel outside off, shaping away with extra bounce. JJ Smuts stays back and pushes at it with hard hands but only manages to get a thick outside edge towards first slip, where Jamie Overton moves to his left to reverse cup it sharply above his head. Italy are 1/2, needing 202 runs in 114 balls.
Commentary.Howout: c Jamie Overton b Jofra Archer

Commentary.Commentary: Two balls down in the chase and Italy have already lost their first wicket. JJ Smuts walks in at number 3, replacing Anthony Mosca.

OUT! TAKEN! Early strike from Jofra Archer. He bangs this into the pitch at 146 clicks, on off. Anthony Mosca decides to take him on straightaway and goes for the pull shot. However, the ball gets big on him and takes the top edge. It flies behind mid on, where Harry Brook turns back, sprints, keeps his eyes on the ball and takes a good catch over his right shoulder. A golden duck for Anthony Mosca after his fine knock against Nepal.
Commentary.Howout: c Harry Brook b Jofra Archer
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.2: Jofra Archer to Anthony Mosca, OUT! c Harry Brook b Jofra Archer.

Commentary.Commentary: Italy are up and running in the chase! Jofra Archer starts with a full delivery, on leg. Justin Mosca looks to flick it but falls over a bit. It goes off the inside edge onto his pads and rolls towards square leg. A single taken.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.1: Jofra Archer to Justin Mosca, 1 run.
